message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that’s done only once every few years. In practice, the entire structure is repainted roughly every seven years, and the actual work takes about **two months**.

Here’s why:

| Factor | Details |
|--------|---------|
| **Height** | 324 m (1,063 ft) |
| **Surface area** | Roughly 10 000 m² of metal |
| **Paint used** | About 60 tons of special anti‑rust paint |
| **Crew size** | ~200 workers (including painters, riggers, safety crews) |
| **Schedule** | Work is scheduled during the off‑peak tourist season (usually late winter/early spring) to minimize disruption |
| **Duration** | 8–10 weeks of continuous work, plus a few days for prep and cleanup |

So if you’re wondering how long it would take to paint the Eiffel Tower from start to finish, expect a two‑month window of intensive, coordinated effort—just like the real thing!
